items.title: Scott Yanow interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021
items.q: I was very happy to turn to page 233 under Nancy Wilson and see my favorite LP of all time, the one she did with Cannonball.

ctx.x: Well you know you can’t have an attitude in your writing. I mean there are some writers like I feel like I need a dictionary to figure out what they’re talking about. And that’s not what you’re aiming for. I use small words. I mean my vocabulary is not that large. If I have to know French to try to be able to figure out what they’re saying then they’ve failed.

Okay. Well speaking of words, I wanted to ask you about I’ve recently been reading your Jazz Singers book and by the way, now I own two copies because Jeannie Cheatham sent me your book. So she must have liked what you wrote about her. And a couple of things I wanted to mention, I was very happy to turn to page 233 under Nancy Wilson and see my favorite LP of all time, the one she did with Cannonball. The other thing I enjoyed was your talk about what makes a jazz singer. And if you don’t mind I wonder if you…

It’s always a tricky thing because with jazz there’s a lot of instances where it’s borderline. Is Rosemary Clooney a jazz singer? Well she sings jazz tunes and she swings. But does she improvise much? You know one could debate about that. And of course one always debates about Frank Sinatra and Tony Bennett. Are they really jazz singers? Well sort of and sort of not. You know. Where someone like Kurt Elling or Betty Carter or Mel Torme, they’re definitely jazz singers. So I mean the quality that is needed is that…
